release_gates.title: Signed fill/lot/value/fees/realized-PnL ledger shared by entries, exits, GTT children and risk state
met: Immutable signed increments with average-cost replay: kite_execution_increments.
Inventory, average cost, fees and realized PnL derived in ONE BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction at synchronous=FULL: kite_inventory.
Duplicate, older-cumulative and reordered evidence converge; a crash before projection books neither quantity nor value.
Corrections and order-identity contradictions are quarantined in kite_execution_conflicts, never applied and never dropped.
Journal entries (execution_lifecycle._book_entry) and broker exits (monitor._book_exit) settle in it.
Partial exits now book their realized PnL instead of setting pnl_reconciliation_required.
state.daily_realized_pnl / _strict — the INR daily-loss breaker input — sum the ledger; the ledger read is deliberately not exception-swallowed, so it cannot fail open.
Quarantined evidence blocks automatic entries via autoexec_preflight.
Lot size is recorded on every increment from the instrument's own payload and projected onto the holding (Inventory.net_lots); quantity remains the unit for all value and risk figures.

Broker charges are fetched per order from /charges/orders and recorded against that order's fills; a cost may not be recorded without provenance, and Inventory.realized_is_gross reports whether the realized figure is still gross of costs.
Exchange timestamps from the postback drive replay ordering; a missing one records 0 rather than an arrival time posing as ordering information.

The exit path distinguishes BOOKED / ALREADY / ABSENT / UNKNOWN. Only ABSENT reaches the legacy single-price accumulator, so an unreadable ledger or evidence it already holds can no longer be double-booked into the daily-loss breaker; UNKNOWN books nowhere and blocks auto-entry.
not_met: GTT children are still unattributed: a trigger's child order carries neither our exit order id nor our tag, so it never reaches the exit path at all. Attribution needs either a broker-verified tag on the GTT order parameters or a get_gtts() correlation pass, and belongs to P0 row 3. Not attempted blind: an unrecognised field on a protective-stop request could fail the stop.
Charges are best effort. A failed /charges/orders call leaves the holding gross of costs; nothing retries it yet.
Positions whose entry predates the ledger, and all paper positions, still book through the legacy single-price accumulator.
No process-level fencing (P0-2): concurrency is proven across threads on one SQLite database, not across engine workers.

test_limitations: Protocol fixtures are not market-performance evidence.
Ledger concurrency is proven with threads against one SQLite file; it does not certify multiple engine processes.
The crash test injects a failure inside the ledger transaction; it is not a process kill.
No live broker, no live order and no real fill was involved in any check here.
The /charges/orders response shape is exercised through a fixture, not against Zerodha.

review_methods: targeted source reads of the execution modules
graph.limitation: The graph answered orientation only; the execution-path reasoning came from reading the modules.
